newsitem.title: POLAND: Taiwan delegation seeks to boost Polish trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan delegation seeks to boost Polish trade.

text.p: A Taiwan delegation agreed with Polish business groups on Thursday to step up bilateral trade exchanges and appealed for Warsaw to back Taipei's bid to join the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"Considering Poland is a member of the WTO, we sincerely believe you will support our application for membership of that organisation," Ho Yuen-Guei, a foreign trade board official of Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs, told an economic cooperation conference in Warsaw.

The two sides agreed to increase the number of bilateral trade and investment missions, exchange information and study a project to set up a centre promoting Taiwan's machinery products, organisers said.
Ho said Poland was Taiwan's chief partner in Central and Eastern Europe, with bilateral trade of $306 million in 1995 and a Polish surplus of $29 million.

Poland accounted for less than 1.4 percent of Taiwan's trade, but its position between east and west Europe made it a potential gateway to the continent and Taipei planned economic missions early next year to study opportunities, he said.
Taiwan's 22-member mission was jointly led by Political Vice Minister of Economic Affairs Chang Chang-pang and included bankers and business representatives.
Poland has diplomatic ties with Beijing rather than Taipei. Its delegation was organised under the Chamber of Commerce (KIG) and headed by Chamber President Andrzej Arendarski.
Vice minister of Foreign Economic Relations Wanda Samborska and Warsaw's mayor, Marcin Swiecicki, spoke at the annual conference, the third since 1994.
Taiwan wants join the Geneva-based WTO in 1997, but faces U.S. and other Western opposition over trade barriers as well as Beijing's determination not to allow the island's entry before its own.
